title: fix(desktop): custom backend skins don't persist across restarts
text: ## What happens Custom skins defined in ~/.hermes/skins/*.yaml (like trt, ares, or any user-created skin) don't survive a desktop restart. The user has to manually run /skin after every launch even though: 1. display.skin is correctly set in config.yaml 2. The desktop persisted the skin name to localStorage in the previous session ## Root cause normalizeSkin() in apps/desktop/src/themes/context.tsx rejects any theme name not currently in the live theme registry. Backend skins are registered *asynchronously* after the gateway connects, so on boot the name is always rejected → falls back to DEFAULT_SKIN_NAME (nous). Then gateway.ready seeds the skin with apply: false (by design — "never stomp the user's persisted desktop theme"), so it stays on nous until the user re-applies manually. PR #69533 fixed WS fan-out and missed-activation recovery for skin.changed events, but doesn't address…

title: Desktop theming is capped by hardcoded CSS knobs, a fixed Shiki theme, and a 4-token syntax schema
text: The desktop app's theme system can't produce some basic looks, and the limits are hardcoded, not just missing polish. Tested with a full custom DesktopTheme contributed via THEMES_AREA plus a skin: 1. **Accent-mix knobs are hardcoded in styles.css and unreachable from themes.** --theme-row-active-accent-mix: 8%, --theme-row-hover-accent-mix: 4%, --theme-control-active-accent-mix: 8%, and (dark) --theme-mix-bubble: 46% are fixed values. A bright userBubble renders as near-background navy because the bubble mixes the seed at 46% toward the dark neutral. Workaround is a plugin-injected CSS override that must match :root.dark specificity — theme authors shouldn't need that. 2. **Code-block colors ignore the active theme entirely.** shiki-highlighter.tsx hardcodes SHIKI_THEME = { dark: 'github-dark-dimmed' }, which follows only the document color-scheme. No theme can change syntax colors in…

title: [Bug]: Inline code in async-delegation/cron result messages renders fixed dark ink on every dark theme (system-message surface misses the themed code rule)
text: ## Summary Inline code spans inside **system-message surfaces** — the [ASYNC DELEGATION BATCH COMPLETE] envelope and cron job outputs — render with Tailwind Typography's fixed near-black ink on **every dark theme**. Body text is correctly theme-colored; only inline code goes dark-on-dark. Normal assistant prose and thinking blocks in the same transcript render correctly. ## Root cause The themed inline-code rule is scoped to the assistant slot only (apps/desktop/src/styles.css, ~line 1895): css [data-slot='aui_assistant-message-content'] .aui-md :not(pre) > code { background: var(--ui-inline-code-background); color: var(--ui-inline-code-foreground); } SystemMessage (src/components/assistant-ui/thread/system-message.tsx, the asyncResult branch) renders delegation results via MarkdownTextContent under [data-slot='aui_system-message-root'] — so the rule never matches there. title: Desktop startup ignores display.skin for backend-authored/user skins
text: ## Bug: Desktop startup ignores display.skin for backend-authored/user skins ### Environment - OS: Linux (Ubuntu) - Hermes Desktop + Hermes core installed via hermes update on latest main - Desktop and backend running on same host ### Steps to reproduce 1. Place a user skin at ~/.hermes/skins/customskin.yaml (any non-built-in skin). 2. hermes config set display.skin customskin 3. Close and reopen Hermes Desktop. ### Expected Desktop launches already painted with the customskin palette. ### Actual Desktop launches in the default nous theme.
